technique.murim.twenty_four_plum_full_bl: 24-Movement Plum Blossom Sword: Plum Blossoms in Full Bloom

Hold R: rooted, sword pointed at one foe. Red blossoms press forward for 6–8 blocks. Projectiles, waves and rushes drain a finite reserve; stronger techniques break the front. Release R: one heavy petal pass through the reached area, then every blossom vanishes. Flank the master or outlast the front.
book.murim.six_harmonies: Six Elements Sword is the first teaching of Mount Hua. Foot accords with knee, waist with shoulder, breath with intent. Raise the blade above your head and bring it straight down upon the foe, lending the blow your body's weight. Do not reach with arms alone: the step must carry the sword, and the exhalation complete its course. This simple art teaches a firm foundation. Yet remember: a raised shoulder betrays the blow before steel falls. Do not stand before the foe with your sword held high.
book.murim.seven_plum_basic: Seven Plum Blossoms Sword grows from the foundations of Mount Hua swordsmanship. No blossom grows without a sturdy branch: first learn to cut, thrust, and return the blade to your chest. Guide the point from the waist. Join your blows with even breathing and small steps. Let each stroke prepare the next, while the free hand keeps your balance. Do not chase a beautiful trail. The sword's blossom opens only where steel can reach; if the foe retreats, first close the distance, then continue the sequence. Forms open by the art's stars, all together: Rush at 1, Whirlwind 3, Execution 5, Shower 7, Explosion 9, and at 11 the peak, Cut and Palisade.
book.murim.seven_plum_blossoms: Settle into your stance, gather your breath, and unfold seven blossoms of the blade before you. Strike along the chosen line before the foe retreats.
book.murim.seven_plum_whirlwind: Circle the blade around your body, raising a ring of pillars. Hold the circle's heart as their walls draw together and imprison the foe.
book.murim.seven_plum_execution: Gather images of the swordsman around a chosen point and send them into a converging strike. Choose ground where the foe will linger.
book.murim.seven_plum_rush: Gather your breath at length in a motionless stance, then release a hurricane of blades straight ahead. Align the path of your onslaught beforehand.
book.murim.twenty_four_plum_rainfall: Raise the sword and call down a shower of cutting petals from the sky. Keep the foe close beneath open heavens, or the blossoms will scatter.
book.murim.falling_petal_sword: Falling Petal Sword belongs to the art of Mount Hua: the petal yields to the wind, yet still finds the earth. Begin your advance from the side. Step in a circle to the left, passing around the foe toward his back. The blade must follow the turning waist, so the feet's motion flows into the blow without a needless swing. Do not halt before another's point or change your arc midway. A brief pause follows the turn; if the foe has gone the other way, recover your stance before closing again.
book.murim.dark_fragrance_step: Dark Fragrance Step is a lightness art of Mount Hua. As plum fragrance passes between branches, the swordsman slips through danger in a short dash. Lower the waist slightly, shift your weight onto the leading foot, and exhale with the push. Your gaze must choose the resting place before your feet leave the earth. Do not mistake swiftness for readiness: after the dash, the body needs a moment to gather its stance again. Leave room for this recovery.
book.murim.dark_fragrance_trail: The Fragrance Trail carries on Mount Hua's lightness art. Gathered breath bears the swordsman forward in a swift, unbroken run, like fragrance following a mountain path. Lean your body, keep your stride even, and choose a clear way ahead. Once you have crossed the needed distance, quiet your strength and end the run by your own will. Do not wait for a wall to end the path. A straight trail is seen from afar: a watchful foe will know your course and meet you with steel.
book.murim.dark_fragrance_behind: Fragrance Behind the Back is Mount Hua's circling step. Choose a foe with your gaze and guide your breath along an arc, moving swiftly to his back. Do not turn the shoulders alone: feet and waist must carry the whole body around him. Keep your sword ready for the next action from the moment you begin. Remember, watchful eyes can follow the arc, and the foe may meet you at its end. With no chosen foe, this art gives only a short step forward.
book.murim.wind_god_steps: The Lightning Flash Step is the short dodge of the Four Strides of the Wind God. Choose a side, or step back if you choose none, and the blow lands where you no longer stand: three blocks at the first star, up to seven at the summit. Higher stars add a brief moment at the start of the flash in which you cannot be struck. The flash costs little qi but leaves you open for a breath afterwards, and it shares one mastery with the other three forms. Do not flash into a wall or into a second foe.
book.murim.wind_god_shadow: %1$s vanishes into dark wind. Move 60–140%% faster until you attack or shadow ends. In combat, 2/2/3/4/5/6 decoys at stars 1/3/5/8/10/12 run at nearby enemies and draw pursuit. Each dies on one hit or after 4–6 s; from star 8 it strikes once for 2 damage with a 10-tick stagger. Your first strike against an enemy fighting a decoy deals +50%%. Outside combat, movement leaves fading afterimages. The observer table limits how many enemies the shadow can fool.
book.murim.wind_god_death: Breach (unlocks at star 3): %1$s dashes through a target in your cone, ending 1.25 blocks behind it, facing it. One armor-piercing strike: main-hand damage ×(1 + 0.05 per star above 3). Breaks guard for 60 ticks and disables shields. Exposed lasts 3 s: +40%% damage from you at star 3, rising to +80%% at star 12; cannot block or parry. Your next accepted technique within 1.5 s has no wind-up. Chains to a second enemy within 5 blocks at star 8, a third at star 12. No target: a plain 4-block charge. Walls stop you.
book.murim.wind_god_lightning: The Star Light Step is the sustained run of the Wind God. Gather speed over the first second and keep a clear route ahead. Mastery improves speed, duration and qi efficiency; ten stars give 30 blocks per second after acceleration. Body training extends the run, and pill discounts still apply. A strike or exhausted qi ends the run. Rest briefly before starting again. The Lightning Flash Step, the dodge, is a separate form sharing this mastery.
book.murim.style.wind_god: The Four Strides of the Wind God is an art of four steps: the Lightning Flash Step, a short dodge; the Dark Shadow Step, which conceals your approach; the Underworld King Step, which advances through an opening; and the Star Light Step, a fast sustained run. One reading teaches all four, and they share one mastery: practice any form to improve the whole art, and greater mastery reduces qi expenditure. The tenth star completes the art: the Star Light Step accelerates for one second, then reaches 30 blocks per second before external bonuses. Choose a clear path. Obstacles still stop you and your qi is finite.
book.murim.style.dark_fragrance: Floating Dark Fragrance Steps are the lightness art of Mount Hua: as plum fragrance passes between the branches, the swordsman passes through danger. Three forms: Slipping Petal, a short dodge; Fragrance Trail, a swift unbroken run; and Fragrance Behind, a circling step to the back of a chosen foe. One reading teaches all three, and they share one mastery: practice any form to improve the whole art. The steps do not replace the sword. They bring it to the right place before the foe.
book.murim.demon_palm: Demon Destruction Palm is a cruel art of the Demonic Sect. It gathers inner strength in the palm and releases it through a close blow. Root your feet, turn your waist, and carry force from the belly through the shoulder to the heel of the palm. Keep the fingers together and the wrist straight; do not push with arms alone. First enter touching distance, then unfold your strength. This art offers no distant strike: a palm extended into empty air leaves you open to the answer.
book.murim.seven_plum_blossoms.full: Before the plum can blossom, the branch must become still. Root your feet, quiet your shoulders, and gather breath at the hilt. Then unfold the blade's blossoms before you and bring their cuts together along the chosen line. Do not seek the foe with your point once they open: the blow's path is already laid. Strike as he finishes a step or is forced to stand and fight. One who knows this stance will move aside before the flowering. Hide your preparation behind his swing, and do not stand exposed without need.
book.murim.seven_plum_whirlwind.full: Guide the sword around your body, like wind circling an ancient plum tree. Pillars will rise from the turning motion, and walls between them will begin to close. Hold the center yourself: from there, you can press the foe toward the narrowing edge and hinder his escape. Do not expect the ring to become a prison at once. While gaps remain between the walls, a nimble foe can leave the circle. Begin the whirlwind where his steps are already confined, and keep him within until it closes. Long flowering demands patience.
book.murim.seven_plum_execution.full: Do not pursue the body; choose the ground where it will linger. Gather images of the swordsman around that place and direct them inward. Their blades will converge like branches above a narrow trail, leaving little room for defense. Yet the image obeys intent, not sight: it will strike the appointed point even after that point is empty. Catch the foe after a heavy swing, beside an obstacle, or in a cramped passage. One who leaves the gathering place in time will leave your swordsmen only dust.
book.murim.seven_plum_rush.full: For the onslaught, stand motionless and gather breath at length, allowing no tremor in the point. Align the path beforehand: the released hurricane of blades will rush straight ahead and will not turn after the foe. Let your gaze measure the passage, not his face. This form best meets one who advances toward you or is confined by walls. On open ground, preparation betrays your intent. Seeing the stance, the foe has time to leave its path. Do not release stored strength into emptiness merely because you have waited long.
book.murim.twenty_four_plum_rainfall.ful: Raise the sword as though opening a road to heaven for the branches, and summon a shower of cutting petals. The blossoms fall from above; fight where no roof shelters the foe. Stay close and press him with short blows, denying him escape from the rain. Do not trust heaven's cut at every distance: far away, the images lose their shape and scatter. Beneath a roof, the petals cannot reach flesh. Draw the foe beneath open skies before raising your blade.
book.murim.ceremonial_draw: The nameless master taught: a sheathed sword is like a word still held back. Quiet your shoulders, hide intent within your breath, and let the foe approach. Then the scabbard releases steel, and the draw cuts the space before you before he recognizes the blow. Do not adorn the motion with a bow: silence performs the rite. Yet remember the price of resolve. Once begun, the draw cannot turn aside. If the foe leaves the blade's path, your hand will finish its promise, and his answering blow will find you.
book.murim.crescent_sweep: The nameless master likened this sweep to a sickle above an autumn field. Guide the blade in a broad arc before you to reach those pressing from different sides. Do not chase every point: one motion meets all who enter its reach. Strength rises from the body's turn; the hand merely guides the harvest. Yet the sickle bares the reaper's chest. The broad arc lowers your guard. One who waits beyond the blade's reach can step inside and strike before your sword returns.
book.murim.shadow_step: The nameless master said: the shadow conquers distance while the eye seeks the body. Gather your breath, slip from your former place, and arrive where the foe has yet to ready his blade. This step serves both approach and escape: change your position before another's steel completes its course. Do not take disappearance for invulnerability. At the step's end, your flank lies open: the foot has found earth while the body still follows. If the foe guesses where you will appear, his weapon will meet you before yours meets him.
book.murim.twenty_four_plum_sea: Plum blossoms meet every flying blade, wrap around it and lay it on the ground. The master stands like a root and guides the sea with his gaze.
book.murim.twenty_four_plum_sea.full: Softness that tames force. A single bud opens on the sword's tip, and blossoms drift from the blade — one, two, then a boundless sea close to the ground. Every arrow and every blade that enters it sinks: a blossom wraps the steel, holds it for a breath and lays it in the grass. Guide the sea with your gaze, but remember: it turns slowly, and its blossoms suffice for only a few projectiles in a volley. The master's feet are rooted and his blade is busy — the sea softens frontal and side melee hits by half, but leaves his back exposed. Whoever holds the sea longer than due pays with blood on his lips.
book.murim.twenty_four_plum_river: Mount Hua's petals surge along the chosen line, sweeping away the foe. While the current gathers, the master stands still, and the sword's path is already fixed.
book.murim.twenty_four_plum_river.full: Mount Hua's sword teaches: a fallen blossom is not dead while wind carries it above the river. Stand still, gather breath, and choose beforehand the path along which the petals will pour. Long silence becomes a torrent of swords: it rushes forward along the appointed line and falls upon the foe who remains before you. Yet the river will not turn after a fugitive. While preparing the blow, your body stands motionless within reach of another's steel. Should the foe leave the chosen path or shelter behind a stone, the fearsome torrent will scatter without reaching him.
book.murim.twenty_four_plum_scatter: Mount Hua's petals ripen in blue flame. Spectral doubles cut the foe's former place; a blow while they gather will scatter the blossoms.
book.murim.twenty_four_plum_scatter.full: Mount Hua's plum scatters its blossoms, and each petal bears the sword's intent. Stand within blue flame, gathering petals until your breath fills them with strength. Then release spectral doubles: they bring their blades down where the chosen foe stood. Thus many images converge in one strike, hiding the true hand among the blossoms. Yet first the flowers must ripen. While gathering, you stand motionless; a foe's blow will interrupt the preparation and break the technique. One who leaves his former place will leave the doubles only emptiness.
book.murim.wedge_fan: The nameless master taught that strength should unfold like a fan in a wanderer's hand. Send sharp wedges spreading forward before you: they reach foes across a broad front and force a tight formation to seek gaps. Do not gather all intent into a single point; let each wedge carry its share of the blow. Thus it is easier to meet advancing foes than pursue a fleeing one. Yet the fan knows no winding paths. The wedges shatter against any obstacle. A foe behind wall or stone will preserve his flesh, while you spend your breath in vain.
book.murim.style.twenty_four_plum: For a hundred years this sword was thought lost. Twenty-four movements are not twenty-four strikes but twenty-four ways to open a flower. Whoever has not passed the Seven Blossoms will see only fine words here. Study in order: each movement is built on the one before, and none forgives haste.
book.murim.seven_plum_explosion: Draw the blade slowly down and back, gathering petals on its tip, then release them in one rising blow as a blast toward the enemy.
book.murim.seven_plum_explosion.full: The seventh form gathers all the earlier ones taught. Draw the blade slowly down and back to your right leg without hurrying the breath: let the qi flow to the tip and the petals fly to it on their own. Hold the sword low for a heartbeat only. Then, with half a step, cut upward through the air, and the whole gathered plum bursts at the top of the blow where the blade looked, even toward an enemy in the sky. But the long wind-up is seen from afar: a sharp-eyed foe leaves the line before the blow, and behind a stone the petals cannot reach him.
technique.murim.seven_plum_shower.weakne: A long coil and a straight dive: break the master in his stance or step off the line of the dive.
book.murim.seven_plum_shower: Coil like a bowstring, push off from afar and pierce the enemy from above: you yourself become the point, and a rain of cuts pours after you.
book.murim.seven_plum_shower.full: Plum Blossom Shower is a thrust in which the whole body becomes the sword. Coil in the stance until light gathers at the hand, and hold it; do not release it early. Push off from afar, rise above the enemy and fall on him at a slant, point first: pass through him, do not stick in him. A shower of parallel cuts pours after you, and below a white flash breaks. A target caught by your gaze freezes even in the sky. The form's weakness is the long coiling and the straight path: it is easier to strike the master in his stance or step off the line of the dive than to withstand the blow.
book.murim.style.seven_plum: The Seven Plum Blossoms Sword is the root of the Mount Hua sword. The blossom does not strike with force: it opens where the enemy does not expect it, and its seven petals are seven ways to open. First learn the style itself: the steps, the grip and the three strikes from which every form grows. Only when the hand stops thinking about the sword will the first form open, and after it the next, each harder than the last. Do not hurry: a blossom opened before its time withers.
technique.murim.tang_five_thunders: Tang Clan: Five Fulgur Chain Strike
technique.murim.tang_five_thunders.weakn: The blades fly straight and aim at the moment of release: a sidestep between them breaks the chain. The throw weakens with distance.
technique.murim.tang_twelve_daggers.weak: A long motionless preparation; a dagger stops at the first body and at walls; the twelfth from the sky is announced by the master's leap.
technique.murim.tang_seven_stars: Tang Clan: Seven Star Soul Exile
technique.murim.tang_seven_stars.weaknes: The net is open toward the master: when the stars flare, step forward and the blades meet behind you. Stone across a qi thread drops its star.
technique.murim.tang_dark_burst.weakness: The slow dagger warns by its writhing and can be struck down; the dash is a straight line; the recall line shows as a qi thread.
book.murim.style.tang_daggers: The Tang Clan of Sichuan carries no sword in sight. Its weapons are blades as thin as willow leaves hidden in the sleeve, and a hand that lets them go before the enemy sees it move. Twelve throws make the art: eleven are known, the twelfth is the family's secret. The chain is counted as Tang Zhan threw it: three blades, then two, then five, and last the eleventh. Learn them in order: each throw stands on the one before it. Remember what is said of the Tang: a thrown blade is hard to call back.
book.murim.tang_five_thunders: Five blades almost at once, fanning out and closing in from different sides on one point: the first meets the guard, the fourth breaks it, the fifth kills.
book.murim.tang_five_thunders.full: Five Fulgur Chain Strike is the fifth throw of the Tang. One whip of the wrist and five blades fan out almost at once, then each turns toward the enemy from its own side. The first meets the guard, the second pushes the blade aside, the third opens a gap, the fourth breaks the defence, the fifth goes for the kill. Lead your hand: all five into one man and the chain breaks his shield; into many and you hold back a crowd. But the farther the enemy, the weaker the throw.
book.murim.tang_twelve_daggers: Eleven blades open in a fan against every foe at once; the twelfth the master throws from above, leaping toward the sun.
book.murim.tang_twelve_daggers.full: The Twelfth Dagger is the summit of the Tang art, Twelve Flying Daggers, and the family's secret. One by one the blades slip from the sleeves and gather between the palms into a spinning flower; the enemy cannot tell which blade is which. A flick of the wrist and the fan opens: the blades fly in arcs, cross each other and find everyone who stands in front. Their edges carry the family's poison. Yet a body or a stone stops a blade, and the long preparation leaves the master open. The twelfth throw is the secret: the master leaps against the sun and strikes from above while the enemy still watches the fan.
book.murim.tang_seven_stars: Seven blades hang like stars behind and beside the enemy and meet in his throat at once: whoever retreats dies.
book.murim.tang_seven_stars.full: Seven Star Soul Exile is the seventh throw, Tang Bo's specialty. The sleeves spread wide and seven blades fly out of both at once. They do not strike at once: they hang around the enemy like the stars of the Dipper and follow him if he backs away. Whoever retreats walks into the stream and takes a blade in the throat. The master decides when the stars fall: earlier is weaker, later is surer. But the net is open on the master's side, and whoever steps forward when the stars flare leaves the meeting point behind his back. Stone across a thread drops its star.
book.murim.tang_dark_burst: A slow dagger writhes like a living carp, then tears forward with the sound of the sky collapsing.
book.murim.tang_dark_burst.full: The Dark Eruption Blade is the eleventh throw. Qi is poured into the blade and it writhes like a living carp, flies slower than rain and raises dust in a whirl, until with the sound of the sky collapsing it tears forward, black and white, and bursts with qi. Throw a second dagger after it: it strikes the first and doubles its momentum. A blade that was deflected or dodged hangs in the air, and the master calls it back along a new line: the Dagger That Severs the Line of Life. The slow blade can be struck down.

technique.murim.tang_three_instant: Tang Clan: Three Blades of One Instant
technique.murim.tang_three_instant.weakn: The blades fly to where you will be: stop or turn back at the moment of the throw and the meeting point is empty. A sidestep does not help.
technique.murim.tang_flash_life.weakness: There is no force in the blade, only speed. Dodge on the master's gesture, not on the blade; a body or stone on the line stops it.
technique.murim.tang_sleeve_return: Tang Clan: Blades Return to the Sleeve
technique.murim.tang_sleeve_return.weakn: Nothing to call back without misses. An enemy is safe if he does not stand on the straight line between the master and the stuck daggers.
book.murim.tang_three_instant: Three blades: one straight, two from the sides and faster; all arrive at the same instant where the enemy will be.
book.murim.tang_three_instant.full: Three Blades of One Instant is the first throw of the Tang. "One came straight at him, and the other two spun toward him from the sides. Those that spun were much faster." The master throws at where the enemy will be, not where he stands: whoever runs or charges walks into all three blades at once, and a sidestep does not help, for arcs close both sides. There is one escape: stop or turn back at the moment of the throw. A deep master bends one of the arcs at a right angle.
book.murim.tang_flash_life: No force in the blade, only speed: it vanishes from the hand and appears right before the enemy's face.
book.murim.tang_flash_life.full: The Flashing Death Strike is the sixth throw. "There was no great force in this dagger. It was simply speed. The dagger vanished as it left the hand and appeared right in front of him." It is not a killing throw but an interrupting one: throw it into the enemy's wind-up and the wind-up breaks. Watching the blade is useless against it: dodge on the master's gesture, on the flick of his fingers. Masters of the highest star send a second blade after the first, one without qi that cannot be sensed.
book.murim.tang_sleeve_return: Your misses are not lost: a dagger that misses sticks in the ground for 15 seconds. Press %1$s and every stuck dagger within 20 blocks flies straight back to you, hitting each enemy on its line.
book.murim.tang_sleeve_return.full: Blades Return to the Sleeve. What to do: when you miss, the daggers stay stuck in the ground, glinting, for 15 seconds. Stand so the enemy is between you and them, then press %1$s. What happens: every stuck dagger within 20 blocks tears free and flies straight back into your sleeve; each one hits any enemy standing on its line. Why: every miss becomes a second hit, and daggers you threw by hand come back to your inventory. Canon, ch. 195: "all the throwing blades lying on the ground were returned to his sleeve."
npc.murim.mentor.title: Master of the White Plum Hall, first-class disciple
npc.murim.leader.title: Leader of the Mount Hua Sect
npc.murim.senior.title: Senior disciple, second generation
npc.murim.disciple.title: Disciple, third generation
dialogue.murim.mentor.outsider: You're not one of ours. Sect books are for disciples. If you want to learn, go to the Leader at the sect gate, at the top of the trail.
dialogue.murim.mentor.who_outsider: Gyeong Pil. Six years now I've taught the children here to hold a sword like a brush. Join, and I'll teach you too.
dialogue.murim.mentor.first:
A new disciple? I am Gyeong Pil, instructor of the White Plum Hall. We will start with the basics.
%s
dialogue.murim.mentor.again: You again. Well, out with it.
dialogue.murim.mentor.opt.lesson: Do you have a lesson for me?
dialogue.murim.mentor.teach: The foundation. The Six Elements, then the Falling Petal, then the first Seven Plum forms. Past that, the world teaches you. I hand over a book when I see the hand is ready.
dialogue.murim.mentor.lessons: A lesson isn't an errand. Do it, and I'll see it myself.
dialogue.murim.mentor.six_given: Make the Six a practiced movement, and reach the third rank yourself. Eight Downward Strikes against the courtyard dummy—carry each one through. Your tablet holds the count.
dialogue.murim.mentor.six_hint: Make the Six familiar. Finish the backswing before the next cut.
dialogue.murim.mentor.six_rank: The hand is ready, the body isn't. You get the Falling Petal when you break into the third rank. Meditate.
dialogue.murim.mentor.six_done:
I see it. Here: the Falling Petal Sword. Read it, then learn. And don't swing it in the kitchen. One more thing: the Leader wants a look at you. Go to him.
%s
dialogue.murim.mentor.spar_given: Go to Seo Rang. Wait for his attack and answer with three clean hits. One bout or several—I will count them all. Then come back.
dialogue.murim.mentor.spar_hint: He's fast because you watch the sword. Watch the shoulder. Let the swing pass, step aside, and strike while he's open.
dialogue.murim.mentor.spar_rank: Three clean ones, I saw. But the Seven Plums burn qi. Break into the second rank, then the book is yours.
dialogue.murim.mentor.spar_done:
Good. Here is the complete Seven Plum Blossoms manual. Pages and practice will deepen the art. Elder Tae Rok asked for you.
%s
dialogue.murim.mentor.beyond: You have the complete Seven Plum curriculum. Practise its forms in order. For the lost Twenty-Four Plum art, ask me about the fragments kept here.
dialogue.murim.mentor.no_dantian: Without a dantian you can't hold qi; the words stay words. Meditate first: build your centre.
dialogue.murim.mentor.secret_locked: You cannot master the full Twenty-Four Movements manual below the Peak. Fragments are another matter: they can restore an incomplete Rainfall, up to its middle layers.
dialogue.murim.mentor.farewell: Go. And tomorrow, on the training ground before dawn.
dialogue.murim.leader.first: A traveller on Mount Hua. Rare, these days. What brings you to the gate?
dialogue.murim.leader.opt.become: I want to become a disciple
dialogue.murim.leader.who: Tae Hwi, leader of this sect. My sword is duller than the elders', but my memory for names is sharper. I'll remember yours too.
dialogue.murim.leader.question: Then one question. Why do you want the sword of Mount Hua?
dialogue.murim.leader.opt.ans_honest: I don't know. I want to find out
dialogue.murim.leader.opt.ans_plum: I want to see the plum bloom
dialogue.murim.leader.reply_strong: Honest, if foolish. Strength without roots breaks first. No matter, the mountain will teach you.
dialogue.murim.leader.reply_protect: A good answer. Remember it when the sword grows heavy.
dialogue.murim.leader.reply_honest: The best answer I've heard this year. Not knowing is an honest door.
dialogue.murim.leader.reply_plum: Ha. The plums here bloom every spring. The sword, less often. We'll see about yours.
dialogue.murim.leader.bow_prompt: The answer is no exam. Now bow to the ancestors of Mount Hua; they watch everyone who enters.
dialogue.murim.leader.after_bow: Good. One last thing: show me a single form of the Six Elements. There's the dummy; strike as you were taught.
dialogue.murim.leader.wait_form: The dummy is still waiting. One form, no more.
dialogue.murim.leader.form_seen: Clumsy. But honest, and the stance holds. That is enough to begin.
dialogue.murim.leader.opt.accept: Take the name of a disciple
dialogue.murim.leader.welcome: From today, you are a third-class disciple of Mount Hua. Go to Gyeong Pil; he will start you on the Six Elements Sword. Then get a meal at the dining hall.
dialogue.murim.leader.member: Ah, a disciple. How goes the training?
dialogue.murim.leader.sect_state: The roof leaks, the treasury is empty, a handful of disciples. But I know each of them by name and by handwriting. That's where we start.
dialogue.murim.senior.outsider: A stranger in the yard? Since you're here, can you hold a sword?
dialogue.murim.senior.greet: Junior. Back again? Itching for it?
dialogue.murim.senior.opt.lesson: The master said: three clean strikes
dialogue.murim.senior.accept: To half strength, then we bow. Don't go crying to the master after.
dialogue.murim.senior.accept_lesson: Clean ones, is it? Then wait for my swing. If you're quick enough.
dialogue.murim.senior.refused1: Cowardice is a choice too. Just don't make it a habit.
dialogue.murim.senior.refused2: As you wish. The yard isn't going anywhere.
dialogue.murim.senior.refused3: Refuse today, and I'll write it down anyway. In the notebook. For myself.
dialogue.murim.senior.refused4: The door isn't shut. Come when your hand stops shaking.
dialogue.murim.senior.refused5: Fine. But a sword rusts while you decide.
dialogue.murim.senior.refused6: The bout won't run away. Only you will.
dialogue.murim.senior.after_won: …Not bad. I yielded fairly. Don't let it go to your head; tomorrow will be different.
dialogue.murim.senior.after_lost: You watch the blade; watch the shoulder. Catch your breath and come again.
dialogue.murim.disciple.line1: The master got us up before dawn again. My legs aren't mine anymore.
dialogue.murim.disciple.line2: They say bandits were seen on the trail again.
dialogue.murim.disciple.line3: A hundred strikes on the dummy, then another hundred. That's the Six Elements.
dialogue.murim.disciple.line4: Don't let Senior Seo Rang catch you after lunch.
dialogue.murim.disciple.line5: The Leader was counting coins again. Porridge for supper, then.
dialogue.murim.disciple.line6: Someday our plum will bloom too. That's what the master says.
murim.sect.joined: You have joined Mount Hua as a third-class disciple.
murim.sect.trial_form: The Leader nods: the form counts.
murim.sect.clean_done: Three clean strikes on the senior. Tell the master.
murim.sect.no_mountain: Mount Hua isn't in this world yet.
dialogue.murim.senior.parting: Seo Rang returns the bow: "Until tomorrow."
npc.murim.gatekeeper.title: Gatekeeper, third generation
dialogue.murim.gatekeeper.outsider: Halt, traveller. This is the foot of Mount Hua. Past here there's only the trail and your own two feet.
dialogue.murim.gatekeeper.opt.become: I want to join Mount Hua
dialogue.murim.gatekeeper.climb: You want to be a disciple of Mount Hua? Climb the mountain yourself; at the sect gate they will hear you out.
dialogue.murim.gatekeeper.far: A thousand steps up the cleft, then the ridge to the Golden Lock. Whoever gets there without turning back is already half one of us.
dialogue.murim.gatekeeper.no_carry: Carry you? Ha. The mountain tests you before the Leader does. Whoever can't climb it can't lift the sword either.
dialogue.murim.gatekeeper.member1: Ah, one of ours. Good road, fellow disciple. They're arguing about rice up top again.
dialogue.murim.gatekeeper.member2: Fellow disciple! Back before supper and I'll save you a flatbread.
dialogue.murim.mentor.where_leader: The head receives disciples at %1$s. I can take you there and introduce you.
dialogue.murim.leader.first_climbed: You climbed on your own, up the steps and not on someone's back. That's half the answer already. What brings you to the gate?
dialogue.murim.leader.where_mentor: Gyeong Pil is %s. Go; he is already waiting for new disciples.
technique.murim.tang_family_coins.weakne: Coins are light: a counter-swing of a weapon knocks them away, and a shield in front stops them. In open ground with nothing to bounce off and a single enemy, the coins are weak.
book.murim.tang_family_coins: Press %1$s for a fan of bronze coins. A coin bounces off walls and floor, and from star 7 it hops to the next enemy after a hit.
book.murim.tang_family_coins.full: Tang Family Coins. Canon, ch. 210: "a technique that used coins; in the past only the heads of the Tang family could learn it." What to do: throw the fan at a wall next to the enemy or into a crowd. What happens: each coin hits for a little, ricochets off blocks (once from star 5, twice from star 9) and hops to a neighbour (from star 7). The fan grows: 3, 7, 12 and finally 18 coins. Why: it is the only Tang form that comes around corners and hits several enemies at once. Coins do not stick in the ground and do not come back.

junk.murim.seal.1: The seal of %1$s is stamped upside down. Twice.
junk.murim.seal.2: The seal of %1$s. One character is written so badly that even a first-year disciple would know better.
junk.murim.seal.3: The seal of %1$s. Beside it, in tiny writing: "Genuine seal. I swear."
junk.murim.seal.4: The seal of %1$s. The ink is fresh and smells of a tavern.
junk.murim.seal.5: The seal of %1$s. Under it someone tried to scrape off another mark: a junk dealer's stamp.
junk.murim.fake.intro.0: Whoever reads this book to the end will become first under heaven. Whoever does not will become second.
junk.murim.fake.intro.1: An immortal passed this art to me in a dream and asked me to tell no one. Selling cheap. — %2$s
junk.murim.fake.intro.2: "%1$s" is a treasure three sects fought over for a hundred years. That is why the book is so thin: they took the rest.
junk.murim.fake.intro.3: Master this art and you can split a mountain. The author would demonstrate, but the villagers are rather fond of theirs.
junk.murim.fake.intro.4: Recorded by %2$s. Tested on three disciples; two are still alive.
junk.murim.fake.intro.5: A hundred years ago, every master in murim knew this technique. Now only the author knows it, and he is very busy.
junk.murim.fake.intro.6: Warning: this art is so powerful that you should read its manual sitting down. Preferably lying down.
junk.murim.fake.intro.7: Found in an ancient master's cave. For some reason, the ink is still wet. — %2$s
junk.murim.fake.step.0: Take your stance. The stance must be invincible.
junk.murim.fake.step.1: Guide qi from the lower dantian to the upper, then back, then somewhere else.
junk.murim.fake.step.2: Swing the sword ten thousand times. If you have no sword, buy one from the author; the shop is by the south gate.
junk.murim.fake.step.3: Imagine a dragon. Now imagine you are the dragon. Strike.
junk.murim.fake.step.4: Hold your breath until you see the truth. If you see your ancestors instead, exhale.
junk.murim.fake.step.5: Deliver a strike that cannot be blocked. For instructions, see the next volume.
junk.murim.fake.step.6: Become the wind. The wind does not study, so you may stop reading here.
junk.murim.fake.step.7: Do all of the above, but faster.
junk.murim.fake.step.8: There should be a diagram here, but the copyist could not draw. He wrote "whoosh" instead.
junk.murim.fake.step.9: Clench your fist so the qi does not leak out. The qi leaked out. Start again.
junk.murim.fake.end.0: If the art failed, your sincerity was insufficient. Another three silver taels should prove it.
junk.murim.fake.end.1: The author tore out the last pages so that no one would become stronger than him.
junk.murim.fake.end.2: The rest is with my disciple. The disciple ran away.
junk.murim.fake.end.3: If you have mastered this, do not boast. Murim has no patience for upstarts.
junk.murim.fake.end.4: The price of this book is three silver taels. If you found it for free, you owe the author three taels.
junk.murim.beggar.head.0: Notes of the Beggar under the East Bridge
junk.murim.beggar.head.1: What the Beggars' Sect Knows (Not Everything)
junk.murim.beggar.head.2: An Old Beggar's Booklet. Do Not Touch: Fleas
junk.murim.beggar.line.0: At %1$s the scraps come out after the third watch. The cook is kind; the dog is not.
junk.murim.beggar.line.1: Young masters from the orthodox sects give generously if you call them "heroes".
junk.murim.beggar.line.2: A Wudang Taoist gives little but delivers a sermon. You cannot eat a sermon.
junk.murim.beggar.line.3: Two masters fought at %1$s yesterday. I picked up a silver button and half a boot.
junk.murim.beggar.line.4: Rumors are worth more than rice. Rice is worth more than I am.
junk.murim.beggar.line.5: The Mount Hua disciples are out in black again, beating bandits. The bandits give less now.
junk.murim.beggar.line.6: To a new member of the Beggars' Sect: never wash. Nobody pities a clean beggar.
junk.murim.beggar.dog.0: Dog-Beating Staff, first form: hit the dog. Second form: hit the dog again. The elder never showed the other forms.
junk.murim.beggar.dog.1: The Dog-Beating Staff teaches one essential lesson: the dog always comes back.
junk.murim.beggar.dog.2: If there is no dog, the Dog-Beating Staff is good for stirring soup.
junk.murim.cook.intro.0: Do not trust the title. These are the recipes of the training hall kitchen, and they beat any technique.
junk.murim.cook.intro.1: The owner wanted a fearsome title to scare off thieves. Now even thieves who cannot read try to steal it.
junk.murim.cook.intro.2: A cook from Mount Hua taught me this. He said the disciples there are always hungry.
junk.murim.ingr.4: noodles rolled out with a sword
junk.murim.ingr.7: one pill (if you can spare it)
junk.murim.ingr.8: tofu from the market by the south gate
junk.murim.cook.step.0: Heat the pot as though you were about to make a breakthrough.
junk.murim.cook.step.1: Cut quickly and do not think of swords. Think of swords and you will cut yourself.
junk.murim.cook.step.2: Simmer until the disciples start peeking into the kitchen.
junk.murim.cook.step.3: Do not pour qi into the soup: the elder will notice.
junk.murim.cook.step.4: Stir to the left, as in the Falling Petal Sword. It tastes better that way. I've tried it.
junk.murim.cook.end.0: If the guest is a murim master, double the pepper: they like to think it is a trial.
junk.murim.cook.end.1: Serve hot. Serve cold to disciples.
junk.murim.cook.end.2: The last recipe is stained with soup. It must have been a good one.
junk.murim.ledger.head.1: Debts and Expenses. For My Eyes Only
junk.murim.ledger.entry.0: Sold a "genuine" manual from %2$s to a young master. Silver received: %1$s.
junk.murim.ledger.entry.1: Bought twenty old covers from a junk dealer. Copper paid: %1$s. Enough for a month's trade.
junk.murim.ledger.entry.2: The same young master came back to complain. Explained that the first volume prepares him to buy the second. Took a deposit.
junk.murim.ledger.entry.3: Payment to the copyist for ten copies of "%3$s": %1$s in copper, plus lunch.
junk.murim.ledger.entry.4: Sold the Six Elements breathing method to a farmer's son for three copper coins. A month later he came back stronger than me. No more genuine stock.
junk.murim.ledger.entry.5: Paid the Beggars' Sect to stay away from the entrance: %1$s in copper.
junk.murim.ledger.entry.6: Disciples of %2$s bought every book with plum blossoms on the cover. Raise prices.
junk.murim.ledger.entry.7: Ink, paper, a radish for the seal. Copper spent: %1$s.
junk.murim.ledger.end.0: Total: profit. Conscience: at a loss.
junk.murim.ledger.end.1: The pages after this are glued together with something sweet.
junk.murim.love.head.1: Poems About Plum Blossoms (Keep Away from Senior Disciples)
junk.murim.love.open.1: Fair maiden of the apothecary's shop,
junk.murim.love.open.2: To the one who trains at dawn by the well,
junk.murim.love.line.0: Today I missed another block in sparring because I was watching you fix your hair.
junk.murim.love.line.1: I swept the courtyard ninety-nine times just to pass your window. The courtyard has never been so clean.
junk.murim.love.line.2: Your sword traces plum blossoms. Mine only digs furrows in the courtyard. If a plum tree grows there, consider it a gift from me.
junk.murim.love.line.3: Senior Brother says love hinders cultivation. Senior Brother has no sweetheart.
junk.murim.love.line.4: When I become a master I will break any villain's sword for you. So far I have only broken my own.
junk.murim.love.line.5: I wrote you a poem: "The plum is blooming. So are you." I could not think of the rest.
junk.murim.love.close.0: Do not reply. I will never dare to send this anyway.
junk.murim.love.close.1: If the elders find this letter, I did not write it.
junk.murim.love.sign.0: Your junior brother, the one who sweeps the courtyard
junk.murim.love.sign.1: The one in the third row at morning drill

junk.murim.heretic.title.2: Sutra of the Nine Inverted Meridians
junk.murim.heretic.intro.0: The orthodox sects teach for years. This method grants power in one night. The price is in small print on the last page.
junk.murim.heretic.intro.1: This method is banned by the Nine Great Sects. There is no better recommendation.
junk.murim.heretic.intro.2: Written in a trembling hand. Probably trembling with power.
junk.murim.heretic.step.0: Send qi through the meridians against the flow. Pain means it is working.
junk.murim.heretic.step.1: Hold your breath for a hundred counts. Do not stop at eighty.
junk.murim.heretic.step.2: Clench the dantian like a fist. Harder.
junk.murim.heretic.step.3: Mix qi with the heart's blood. If your nose bleeds, keep mixing.
junk.murim.heretic.step.4: Do not meditate alone. Have someone nearby who can call a physician.

junk.murim.heretic.margin.2: Brown stains in the margin. That is not ink.

junk.murim.torn.text.2: When the opponent retreats, do not pursue. Wait until his stance
junk.murim.torn.text.3: Twenty-four movements are bound by one thread: the first gives birth to the second, the second
junk.murim.torn.text.4: To pierce protective qi, first find the place where it is thinnest, and that is
junk.murim.torn.text.5: Swing. Strike. Block. Every sword technique under heaven begins with these three words, and it ends with
junk.murim.torn.note.0: [The rest of the page is torn away.]
junk.murim.torn.note.1: [Mice ate the rest. The mice, it seems, grew stronger.]
junk.murim.torn.note.2: [Someone tore out the page and left a note: "I need it more."]
junk.murim.muse.line.0: The plum does not hurry to bloom. But when it blooms, it can be seen from the far side of the valley.
junk.murim.muse.line.1: The disciple seeks a secret technique. The master practises the basics. That is why one is a disciple and the other a master.
junk.murim.muse.line.2: A sword's true weight lies in what it has done.
junk.murim.muse.line.3: The fastest form is the one you no longer have to think through.
junk.murim.muse.line.4: Losing is no disgrace. The disgrace is not understanding why.
junk.murim.muse.line.5: A simple strike, repeated ten thousand times, stops being simple.
junk.murim.muse.line.6: Swing. Strike. Block. Everything else is decoration.
junk.murim.muse.line.7: Whoever rushes to the summit does not see the path. And the path is the teacher.
junk.murim.clue.body.0: A bookcase on the bottom level kept wobbling — the %1$s one from the stairs. Books kept falling off. I wedged an old book under one leg. Rock solid now.
junk.murim.clue.body.1: Inventory. Shelf contents: miscellaneous, dubious. Bottom level, %1$s bookcase from the stairs: one useless book wedged under its leg. Do not remove. The bookcase will fall over.
junk.murim.clue.body.2: On the bottom level is a bookcase — the %1$s one from the stairs. There is a book under one leg. If you want it, find a replacement first. I have put these shelves back together twice.
junk.murim.clue.vague.0: True manuals are hidden where looters do not look: not on the shelves but under them.
junk.murim.clue.vague.1: Old archives were dug deep. The lower the tier, the older the books.
junk.murim.clue.sign.0: — Keeper Yu, the last one in this archive
junk.murim.water.note: The ink has run. Only a few words can be made out.
junk.murim.author: Author: %1$s
junk.murim.look.manual: There are hundreds like it on the shelves: same cover, another title
junk.murim.msg.comprehend: Plain words settle in your heart. You feel something fall into place.
junk.murim.msg.backlash: Your qi flows backward through your meridians. Qi deviation!
junk.murim.msg.backlash_none: You try the method, but without a dantian you have no qi to send astray. You just feel dizzy.
junk.murim.msg.clue: The keeper's note identifies the bookcase propped up with a book.
junk.murim.msg.propped: You pull the hidden manual out from beneath the bookcase and slip an old book under the foot instead.
npc.murim.second.title: Disciple, second generation
npc.murim.elder.title: Elder of Mount Hua
npc.murim.tae_gyun.title: Elder, head of the Finance Hall
npc.murim.tae_rok.title: Elder, head of the Martial Hall
npc.murim.gyeong_cho.title: Head of the Medicine Pavilion, first generation
npc.murim.gyeong_tak.title: First-generation senior, the Leader's right hand
dialogue.murim.disciple.formation1: Shh! Formation. Gyeong Pil is watching — talk later.
dialogue.murim.disciple.formation2: Take the end of a row, there's room. And keep the beat!
dialogue.murim.disciple.formation3: Third form… no, fourth. Don't put me off!
dialogue.murim.disciple.formation4: Straighter, straighter! The mentor is already looking at my corner.
dialogue.murim.disciple.formation5: Counting aloud so I don't fall asleep. One, two...
dialogue.murim.disciple.formation6: Just don't laugh if I miss. I know already.
dialogue.murim.disciple.meal1: Porridge and nuts. Again. They say it hardens the spirit.
dialogue.murim.disciple.meal2: Eat faster — after the bell the master won't wait.
dialogue.murim.disciple.meal3: Elder Tae Gyun put an extra scoop of porridge in my bowl today. Said he doesn't count food, he counts paper.
dialogue.murim.disciple.night1: Mm… dawn's soon. Let me sleep, brother.
dialogue.murim.disciple.night2: No wandering the yard at night. Formation at dawn — you'll oversleep.
dialogue.murim.disciple.evening1: Evening is the only time my legs stop aching. Almost.
dialogue.murim.disciple.evening2: Did you see senior Seo Rang fight today? Like painting a plum branch.
dialogue.murim.disciple.evening3: They say bandits were seen on the trail again.
dialogue.murim.disciple.doing_training1: Spars to half strength, the poles, forms behind the ranks — whatever the master says. Sand for me today.
dialogue.murim.disciple.doing_training2: The plum blossom poles. Fall and you start again. I fell forty times.
dialogue.murim.disciple.doing_training3: Posts in the morning, sand after lunch. By evening I'm all calluses.
dialogue.murim.disciple.doing_training4: I hold the sword with both hands, and it's still heavier. How?
dialogue.murim.disciple.doing_training5: Forms behind the ranks today. Everyone watches, but only the seniors see the mistakes.
dialogue.murim.disciple.doing_training6: Fell off a post. Got up. Fell. Got up. That's the whole training, honestly.
dialogue.murim.disciple.busy1: Not now — I have a bout!
dialogue.murim.disciple.busy2: Later, later! Can’t you see we’re fighting?
dialogue.murim.disciple.busy3: Don't interrupt, my arm is mid-swing!
dialogue.murim.disciple.busy4: Wait, we'll finish, then we talk.
dialogue.murim.disciple.busy6: Wait at the edge. A minute and I'm yours.
dialogue.murim.disciple.opt.challenge: Spar with me? To half strength
dialogue.murim.disciple.challenge: With me? Fine. A bow, then to half strength. Just don't complain to the master.
dialogue.murim.disciple.joined: Go on, at the end. Watch the front row and strike with us.
dialogue.murim.second.formation1: Junior, the ranks are no place for chatter. Fall in or leave.
dialogue.murim.second.formation2: The front row keeps the beat. Watch my sword, not my face.
dialogue.murim.second.formation3: Fall in or leave. There is no middle.
dialogue.murim.second.formation4: The front row does not look away. Neither should you distract it.
dialogue.murim.second.formation5: Quiet. Hear the beat? Land on it.
dialogue.murim.second.formation6: We'll talk later. Now the form.
dialogue.murim.second.meal1: Seniors are served first. Get used to it.
dialogue.murim.second.meal2: I spent a year away from the mountain. Even this porridge feels like luxury now.
dialogue.murim.second.greet1: Junior. A bow to your senior — forgotten how it’s done?
dialogue.murim.second.greet2: Want to ask something — ask briefly. The sword is waiting.
dialogue.murim.second.greet3: Seo Rang was up before everyone again. Unbearable.
dialogue.murim.second.evening1: The grove is quiet in the evening. Qi flows smoother when juniors don’t interrupt.
dialogue.murim.second.evening2: Sit by me, if you can keep quiet.
dialogue.murim.second.night1: Night. Go to sleep, junior. Formation tomorrow.
dialogue.murim.second.busy5: You'll wait. A bout is on.
dialogue.murim.second.busy6: Ask later. No time for words now.
dialogue.murim.second.bowed: Hm. Better. Maybe something will come of you yet.
dialogue.murim.second.challenge: A lesson? Fine. To half strength — and don't say I didn't warn you.
dialogue.murim.tae_gyun.formation1: Dawn formation costs nothing. The best thing this sect has.
dialogue.murim.tae_gyun.opt.ask: How is the sect faring, elder?
dialogue.murim.tae_gyun.night1: Only spendthrifts burn candles at night. And me — over the ledger.
dialogue.murim.tae_gyun.greet1: Money doesn't grow on plum trees, disciple. Though some here seem to believe it does.
dialogue.murim.tae_gyun.greet2: Did you break something? No? Then why come to the Finance Hall?
dialogue.murim.tae_gyun.answer: Debts in Huayin, the old books full of stains and holes, and paper gets dearer. But the sect stands. As long as every entry is honest, it stands.
dialogue.murim.tae_rok.formation1: Watching the ranks. The second row is half a beat behind again.
dialogue.murim.tae_rok.evening1: Evening is for rereading what your hands did by day.
dialogue.murim.tae_rok.greet1: The Martial Hall is open to those who read, not those who flip pages.
dialogue.murim.tae_rok.greet2: Show me your stance. …Shoulder up. Like that.
dialogue.murim.tae_rok.answer: The foundation. The Six Elements — everything begins and ends with a six-part movement. The rest will follow.
dialogue.murim.gyeong_cho.breakfast_dinn: Eat. An empty dantian can't hold qi.
dialogue.murim.gyeong_cho.opt.ask: How do you treat injuries from training?
dialogue.murim.gyeong_cho.night1: At night they bring me those who trained in secret. Don't be one of them.
dialogue.murim.gyeong_cho.greet1: Bruises again? Show me. Hm, you'll live.
dialogue.murim.gyeong_cho.greet2: Herbs drying, the cauldron boiling. There is always work in the Medicine Pavilion.
dialogue.murim.gyeong_cho.answer: Bruise salve and rest. Pills are for meridians, not for idlers who fell off the poles.
dialogue.murim.gyeong_tak.night1: Go to sleep. The gate is shut and the night shift has it. Come back at dawn.
dialogue.murim.gyeong_tak.opt.ask: What does the sect need, senior?
dialogue.murim.gyeong_tak.greet1: The sect gate is watched. The Leader ordered it — I stand.
dialogue.murim.gyeong_tak.greet2: A newcomer? The Leader will receive you himself. And I'll take you to bow to the ancestors.
dialogue.murim.gyeong_tak.answer: People who stay when it gets hard. The rest we will earn.
dialogue.murim.elder.greet1: Study, disciple. The mountain remembers effort.
dialogue.murim.mentor.formation: Dawn. Take the end of any row. Follow the front row, strike for strike. Ten in time will do. A mistake? Your earlier successes still count.
dialogue.murim.mentor.fall_in: Don't watch the sword — watch the shoulder of the man in front. Strike with him.
dialogue.murim.mentor.training: Sand, poles, forms. Everyone has his task. Why are you standing around?
murim.sect.morning.offbeat: Off the beat — watch the front row.
murim.sect.morning.done: Morning training complete: the forms you drilled are learned.
item.murim.manual_page.hint_bind: %s pages of one book bind into a torn manual
item.murim.manual_page.hint_known: A known book: the page continues it or brings insight
murim.page.need_more: %s: %s of %s pages — the text does not make sense yet
murim.page.deepened: %s: the missing page continues the text — now up to star %s
murim.page.insight: %s: an old page shows the familiar form anew
murim.page.wisdom: %s: nothing new, but reading settles the mind
murim.page.reread: %s: rereading a familiar book, you see more than before
murim.page.reread_wisdom: %s: you know this book by heart; reading it again settles the mind
murim.manual.reread_hint: You know all of it. Rereading wears the book out but brings insight.
murim.camp.alarm: The camp bell rings — the bandits are coming!
murim.camp.cleared: The bandit camp is routed. The ruins and loot remain; another band may settle elsewhere in 5–7 days.
command.murim.camp.reset: The camp is reset: the band will return when you come near
murim.sect.guard.warn: %s: "Halt. Beyond here is %s. Not for you yet."
murim.sect.guard.warn_outsider: %s: "Outsiders go no further than the gate. Tell me why you came; a disciple will lead you to the mentor."
murim.sect.guard.block: %s steps into your way: "Back. This is %s."
murim.sect.guard.night: %s: "Who's sneaking there?! No one enters %s at night."
murim.sect.guard.challenge: %s: "If words don't reach you, a sword will." Merit −%s.
murim.sect.guard.expel: %s puts you out beyond the sect gate: "Introduce yourself at the gate first."

npc.murim.steward.title: Steward of the sect's estate: stores, land, shops
npc.murim.cook.title: Dining-hall cook, lay servant
npc.murim.porter.title: Porter, lay servant
npc.murim.gardener.title: Herb-tender of the alchemy pavilion, lay servant
